result.report:
The supplied argument establishes the exact all-K pure-curve recognition theorem, including singularities, nilpotents, unequal actual generic Artinian lengths, imperfect fields and positive characteristic. The conclusions hold on ordinary opens and include every analytic extension and every analytic curve morphism in the published classical definition. Original arbitrary-dimensional P06.2 remains open. No ordinary-smooth approximation theorem is required or established.

I reconstructed the supporting arguments rather than transferring their historical verdicts. The stated Gate R matches n700 Theorem A, and Gate T matches n701’s completed-algebraic transport and compact-test theorems. The main and expanded-wrapper bindings are distinguished correctly. Hashes, compilation and historical receipts were not used as mathematical evidence.

The field construction is valid. The finite-field norm foundation is also reconstructed in n701 from finite Banach-algebra foundations and finite-dimensional norm equivalence. In Lemma 1, the approximating polynomial coefficients remain bounded by R, consecutive root choices have distance at most 2^(-m), and the ultrametric estimate makes the roots Cauchy. Their limit is a root of the original polynomial. This proves algebraic closure without separability or characteristic restrictions. Lemma 2 gives compatible actual isometric embeddings into the completed algebraic closure of L; it does not identify a completed tensor product with a field.

The finite-stage part of n701 is established. Its actual finite tensors, separable minimal-prime calculations and purely inseparable prime correspondence establish componentwise purity. The finite-Galois argument checks the entire residue-field fibre, constructs the needed local intermediate-field structure by Banach Newton iteration, and uses the same-carrier calibration factor only for that structure. The fixed-locus argument does not assume invariant-test descent. Its collar estimates cover all ranks: rank zero gives zero restriction, rank at least two gives volume O(delta^r) against derivatives O(delta^(-2)), and rank one uses the vanishing coefficient to gain O(delta). Thus the differentiated collars have uniformly bounded variation, while the undifferentiated terms tend to zero. Stokes and uniform smooth approximation of the continuous multiplier justify the limiting pairing. Frobenius descent handles every exterior factor in inseparable stages; mixed extensions are then covered.

At completion, sufficiently close approximations preserve each rational system, including its strict locus, exactly. Unit approximations give equality of logarithmic smooth scalar sections, and compact-image nullity plus the derivations gives exact equality of higher forms. The finite-stage cutoff construction produces one global compact test; neither saturation of the original support nor agreement of local representatives on stage overlaps is assumed. The separate purity contradiction descends a hypothetical lower-dimensional rational neighbourhood to a finite stage and contradicts scalar dimension invariance. Points with minimal-prime kernels then establish the dimension of every actual upstairs component. Consequently the measure projection formula applies with the continuous multiplier bounded on compact support. The Artinian identity sums length times residue-field degree and preserves the actual calibrated sum, including nilpotents and inseparability. It introduces no field-degree factor for scalar extension. The optional reverse-current implication in n701 is independently justified by compact pullback tests and the same projection formula.

The n100 supporting proofs are established. The cutting argument uses reduced S1 component cycles, regular functions and positive effective divisor limits; it does not assert that arbitrary intermediate quotients are S1. Its continuous-multiplier limit is justified by positive coefficient-measure bounds. Closed-embedding tests are lifted with actual analytic units, compact cutoffs and zero extensions. The calibrated variation theorem is applied with its compactness, S1, regular one-dimensional target and pure relative-dimension hypotheses established. Successive cuts retain the desired curve with positive multiplicity, and distinct remaining branches meet only in locally finite rigid sets. At a rigid point, the minimal-polynomial norm argument proves local constancy of scalar tests, including inseparable residue fields. Radial cutoffs have uniformly bounded Hessian variation and shrinking support; continuity eliminates the possible point-supported scalar current. Normalization transport therefore follows from the actual isomorphism locus and puncture removal, rather than inversion of a direct image. The generic-length associativity calculation and the optional regular algebraic globalization also have the stated hypotheses and valid derivations.

The n700 recognition proof is established. Connected normal strict affinoid curve neighbourhoods have integral algebras. The embedding theorem is used over the same algebraically closed complete field. The restricted affinoid-category interpretation preserves the algebra, morphism and domain structure. The two separated boundaryless interior equalities then identify actual ordinary neighbourhoods, including at nonrigid analytic points. Wanner is applied only on ordinary opens of smooth proper algebraic curves over its required field. Its algebraic-unit compact tests are included among ordinary analytic CLD tests with the same pairing, which suffices for positivity of both signs. Reduction and normalization use n100 before recognition; finite-surjective GR descent is applied only after harmonicity is recognized. I also checked n700’s additional local-image and ground-field probe proofs: the constant branch factors the entire bounded Tate map, the nonconstant branch checks actual fibres and uses Zariski upper semicontinuity to reach every analytic point, and the finite kernel image and normalization lift are bounded actual analytic constructions.

The new integration establishes every antecedent of both gates: C is an analytic completed-algebraic extension, X_C is an actual good separated strict boundaryless pure curve, and its zero-Hessian equation holds against every ordinary compact scalar test. Gate R recognizes h_C. GR 3.14(6) then detects already-recognized harmonicity over K. Its applicable comparison proof uses harmonic pullback, boundary projection and scalar surjectivity; finite values exclude the minus-infinity alternative. GR 4.1.2 applied to both signs gives the full classical extension-field and curve-map quantifiers. Hence every stated composite is GR-harmonic, and a smooth strict composite is Thuillier-harmonic. This step transports functions, not arbitrary currents.

GR 3.15 applies to the original continuous function on the strict curve over a nontrivially valued field. Its proof chain uses completion of perfection, reduction, normalization, PL descent and numerical-triviality descent within their published hypotheses. GJR’s good/strict/complete/nontrivial field conventions hold, so its numerical criterion establishes GJR harmonicity after R-PL regularity is obtained. Ordinary-open restriction preserves the geometric hypotheses, compact scalar tests extend by zero, and the canonical pairing restricts correctly. The optional GR 4.2(5) route is consistent. The quoted classical finite-map converse 4.2(6) is explicitly unused and supplies no premise to this integration.

Harmless corrections: in the specified GJR v3, the reduction and completed-algebraic PL results cited inside GR 3.15 are Lemma 5.4(3) and Corollary 5.12, respectively; GR’s older labels 5.3(3) and 5.11 should be cross-referenced accordingly. In n700, “strict affinoid domain algebra” for A/I should read “strict affinoid integral algebra” to avoid confusing a closed subspace with an analytic domain. The extracted plus-infinity codomain in GR 3.5(7), missing zero-dimensional condition in CLD 13.3.3’s extracted proof, and damaged summation/Thuillier glyphs are transcription defects; the precise statements and supplied derivations use their correct meanings. None requires a mathematical repair.

Matching primary sources were opened. HAL access and the large Berkovich downloads were restricted by the browser; the supplied primary excerpts were used for those bodies, with the boundary statements additionally checked in accessible CLD and Conrad–Temkin primary texts. No fresh filesystem, byte-hash or build verification is claimed. There is no unsettled indispensable mathematical step in the supplied recognition chain.

If A is reduced, its spectral seminorm is a norm equivalent to its Banach norm. Strict affinoid algebras admit bounded quotient presentations by unit-radius Tate algebras. [CLD 11.1.1–2]

passages.statement: If K is complete and nontrivially valued and A is a strict K-affinoid algebra, the residue field A/m at every maximal ideal m is finite over K. More generally, A/q is finite-dimensional over K when rad(q) is maximal. [BGR 6.1.2/1; Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, 1.4, Proposition 3]

Every point has a basis of such neighbourhoods, and inside any prescribed ordinary neighbourhood the system can be chosen with all corresponding inequalities strict at that point. [CLD 11.1.5]

passages.statement: Every ordinary open in a Berkovich analytic space is an analytic domain with its canonical restricted structure. A good analytic space has an affinoid-neighbourhood basis. Over a complete nontrivially valued field, every point of a good strict analytic space has a strict affinoid neighbourhood. Analytic-domain structures satisfy their stated factorization universal property. [CLD 11.1.5–8, 11.7.7]

domaine analytique.

passages.statement: Analytic dimension is invariant under complete scalar extension and reduction. For a strict affinoid it equals the Krull dimension of its algebra. Local dimension is the maximum dimension of the irreducible components containing the point, and analytic-domain restriction preserves local dimension. [CLD 11.2.3]

Such algebras are k-affinoid. If k is nontrivially valued and A is strict, an existing Banach A-algebra finite as a ring A-algebra has this finite-module topology. [CLD 11.4.4]

passages.statement: Finite analytic morphisms are boundaryless, are stable under composition and analytic base change, and have affinoid inverse images of affinoid domains with finite Banach algebra maps. A morphism is finite at a point precisely when it is finite from an analytic neighbourhood of that point to an analytic neighbourhood of its image. [CLD 11.4.4]

passages.statement: For an analytic-domain inclusion, relative interior is ordinary topological interior. For Z → Y → X, Int(Z/Y) ∩ g^(-1)Int(Y/X) is contained in Int(Z/X), with equality when Y → X is locally separated. Relative interiors satisfy the scalar-base-change inclusion, and boundaryless morphisms are stable under composition and analytic base change. On a pure calibrated analytic tropical space, Stokes holds for compact C1 forms of type (n−1,n). premises: For a k-affinoid algebra A, A is noetherian, every ideal is closed, M(A) → Spec(A) is surjective, and its spectral seminorm vanishes exactly on nilpotent elements. If A is reduced, its spectral seminorm is a norm equivalent to its Banach norm. Strict affinoid algebras admit bounded quotient presentations by unit-radius Tate algebras. [CLD 11.1.1–2]

If K is complete and nontrivially valued and A is a strict K-affinoid algebra, the residue field A/m at every maximal ideal m is finite over K. More generally, A/q is finite-dimensional over K when rad(q) is maximal. [BGR 6.1.2/1; Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry, 1.4, Proposition 3]

For an affinoid space M(A), a rational system |f_i| ≤ r_i|g| with positive real r_i and no common zero of g,f_1,…,f_s defines an affinoid domain with its rational localization algebra. Every point has a basis of such neighbourhoods, and inside any prescribed ordinary neighbourhood the system can be chosen with all corresponding inequalities strict at that point. [CLD 11.1.5]

Every ordinary open in a Berkovich analytic space is an analytic domain with its canonical restricted structure. A good analytic space has an affinoid-neighbourhood basis. Over a complete nontrivially valued field, every point of a good strict analytic space has a strict affinoid neighbourhood. Analytic-domain structures satisfy their stated factorization universal property. [CLD 11.1.5–8, 11.7.7]

Analytic dimension is invariant under complete scalar extension and reduction. For a strict affinoid it equals the Krull dimension of its algebra. Local dimension is the maximum dimension of the irreducible components containing the point, and analytic-domain restriction preserves local dimension. [CLD 11.2.3]

Affinoid analytic spaces have finitely many irreducible components. An irreducible analytic space is pure-dimensional, and its proper Zariski-closed subsets have smaller dimension. Closed analytic subspaces of M(A) are M(A/I), and reduction has the same carrier. [CLD 11.2.2–5]

For a k-affinoid algebra A, forgetting the norm gives an equivalence between finite Banach A-algebras and finite ring A-algebras; the finite-module quotient topology is independent, up to equivalent norms, of the chosen finite presentation. Such algebras are k-affinoid. If k is nontrivially valued and A is strict, an existing Banach A-algebra finite as a ring A-algebra has this finite-module topology. [CLD 11.4.4]

Finite analytic morphisms are boundaryless, are stable under composition and analytic base change, and have affinoid inverse images of affinoid domains with finite Banach algebra maps. A morphism is finite at a point precisely when it is finite from an analytic neighbourhood of that point to an analytic neighbourhood of its image. [CLD 11.4.4]

Normalization of an analytic space is finite and surjective; on affinoids it is obtained from the integral closure of the reduced algebra in its total quotient ring, and normalization is local under domain restriction. [CLD 11.3.1 and the normalization construction]

For an analytic morphism f:Y → X, dim_y(f) is the local dimension of its actual H(f(y))-analytic fibre and is Zariski upper semicontinuous. The morphism is finite at y if and only if dim_y(f)=0 and y belongs to Int(Y/X). [CLD 11.4.5]

For an analytic-domain inclusion, relative interior is ordinary topological interior. For Z → Y → X, Int(Z/Y) ∩ g^(-1)Int(Y/X) is contained in Int(Z/X), with equality when Y → X is locally separated. Relative interiors satisfy the scalar-base-change inclusion, and boundaryless morphisms are stable under composition and analytic base change. Algebraic analytifications over their ground affinoid base are boundaryless. [CLD 11.4.1; Conrad–Temkin, Lemma 2.9; Berkovich 1.5.5]

Regularity and the stated Serre conditions on coherent modules are preserved and detected by analytic-domain restriction. Quasi-smoothness is geometric regularity and is preserved by complete scalar extension. On good spaces, smoothness is quasi-smoothness together with relative interior. [CLD 11.3.1, 11.4.8–9]

A regular element of an affinoid algebra remains regular on every affinoid domain; its nonempty zero space on a pure r-dimensional analytic space is pure of dimension r−1. For a morphism from a pure n-dimensional analytic space to A^d, every fibre point has local fibre dimension at least n−d, with equality when the target point has d_k-invariant d. [CLD 13.6.1, 13.7.1, 11.5.2]

Ordinary CLD smooth forms admit ordinary-local analytic-unit moment presentations with ambient smooth superform coefficients. Closed paralinéaire coefficient spaces have the stated ambient extension property. Compact-image nullity characterizes zero sections. Pullback, exterior products, J, d′ and d″ have the stated sheaf, functoriality, Leibniz and differential identities. [CLD 1.9.4, 3.3.3, 3.3.10–12, 3.4.4, 6.2.1–2, 15.1.1]

On a locally holomorphically separated analytic space, every compact set K inside an ordinary open U has an ordinary smooth cutoff equal to one near K and with compact support contained in U. Good Hausdorff analytic spaces are locally holomorphically separated. [CLD 15.2.2, 15.2.5]

Positive ordinary CLD currents have local Radon-measure coefficients and order zero; multiplication by locally bounded Borel scalar functions is defined. Wedging a positive current with a strongly positive smooth form preserves positivity. [CLD 7.2.7–12]

On a pure calibrated analytic tropical space, Stokes holds for compact C1 forms of type (n−1,n). Green’s formula holds for symmetric C2 forms of types (p,p),(q,q) with p+q=n−1 and compact intersection of supports. On boundaryless spaces, ordinary integration currents commute with differentiation, the fundamental integration current is closed, and current operations satisfy dual differential, Leibniz, weak-continuity and domain-restriction rules. [CLD 5.11.1, 7.1, 7.7, 15.7.1–2]

Smooth CLD top forms determine locally finite signed Radon measures, with positive measures for positive forms, and compact smooth top forms are integrable. Canonical integration on a pure analytic space is integration of its associated cycle with actual generic Artinian lengths; these lengths and canonical calibrations are compatible with analytic-domain restriction. The intrinsic analytic and domain tropical structures coincide. [CLD 5.8.1–5, 13.2.6, 14.3.5, 15.7.1–2, 16.6.3]

The support of an ordinary smooth CLD form of type (p,q) is contained in the locus d_k(x) ≥ max(p,q). Consequently it avoids any closed analytic subset of dimension less than max(p,q). Superforms on a paralinéaire space of dimension less than max(p,q) vanish in that bidegree. [CLD 1.9.9, 15.2.1]

If X is compact and Γ-strict of dimension d and f_1,…,f_s are analytic units, their simultaneous norm image is a c-polytope of dimension at most d; the norm image of the analytic boundary is contained in a c-polytope of dimension at most d−1, where c=(Q,(|k×|·Γ)^Q). [Ducros, Espaces de Berkovich, polytopes, squelettes et théorie des modèles, Theorem 3.2]

For a compact analytic X, an analytic morphism f:X → Y, an analytic-unit moment g, and a rigid y in Y, there are a neighbourhood U of y and a polyhedron Δ contained in g_trop(X_y), of dimension at most dim(X_y)−1, such that g_trop(X_u) is contained in g_trop(X_y) and g_trop(X_u∩∂X) is contained in Δ for all u in U. [CLD 14.7.1]

Let X be compact, pure n-dimensional and S1, let Y be regular and pure one-dimensional, and let f:X → Y be pure of relative dimension n−1. For an analytic-unit moment g and a rigid y in Y, the calibrated (n−1)-dimensional fibre moment image is constant near y. If Y=A^1 and y=0, the calibrated image of the moment (g,f) on f≠0, sufficiently far in the negative log|f| direction, is the product of the calibrated fibre image and the standard interval calibration. [CLD 14.7.2, specialized to d=1]

For a level-n analytic space and an n-dimensional convenient moment cell, a torus projection injective on its tropical image is finite flat of a constant positive degree on the cell interior. Canonical cell calibrations use those actual fibre degrees. Under complete scalar extension, the degrees sum over the scalar-extended fibre points and the pushforward of the canonical skeletal calibration equals the original calibration. [CLD 13.3.1–3, 14.2.2, 14.3.2–6]

For a complete scalar extension L/k and scalar projection p:X_L → X, canonical top-form measures satisfy p_*((p^*ω)_Bor)=ω_Bor, and, for locally integrable ω, p_*((p^*ω)_Rad)=ω_Rad. This is scalar extension with each space’s canonical calibration and has no factor [L:k]. [CLD 15.3.1]

If F/k is a finite valued extension and X is an F-analytic space of level n, viewing X as k-analytic on the same carrier preserves dimension and skeletal subsets, and its k-canonical calibration is [F:k] times its F-canonical calibration. [CLD 14.4.3]

For a Λ-PL function on a good strict analytic space over a complete nontrivially valued field, semipositivity and harmonicity are preserved by analytic morphisms; the global converse holds for proper surjective morphisms. They are also preserved and detected globally by every analytic field extension and by reduction. These detection statements presuppose the stated Λ-PL hypotheses. [GJR Proposition 7.6(1′,2′,3′)]

For a rig-smooth curve over a complete nontrivially valued field, GJR harmonicity in Definition 7.2 is equivalent to Thuillier harmonicity with the convention specified in GJR 15.6. [GJR Proposition 15.7]

A noetherian regular local ring is an integral domain. If its dimension is d and x_1,…,x_d minimally generate its maximal ideal, they form a regular sequence and the quotient by x_1,…,x_c is regular local of dimension d−c for 0≤c≤d. [Stacks Project, Lemmas 10.106.2–3]

Finite-type algebras over a field are excellent and Jacobson; their regular loci are open. Every nonempty closed subset of a finite-type scheme over a field contains a closed point, and the closed points are dense in every closed subset. [Stacks Project, Sections 15.48, 15.53 and 10.35]
